summary.prose: Connect normal code-review requests to the working task-review engine and keep independent reviews isolated. Retain completed review summaries permanently, then delete the story’s temporary checkpoint files only after its BUILD is approved. Daemon reviews survive submitter disconnect; controller reviews require explicit retrigger after loss of their live owner.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary:
Use one task-oriented review coordinator over the existing provider, task and artifact infrastructure. The model reads a task's functional summary, committed Story/LLD/Plan references, selected changed segments and complete test details, investigates as needed, then returns ordinary findings and a task result. The host handles identities, ordering, timing, JSON persistence and CR publication. No model-facing evidence aliases, coverage ledgers, qualification probes, signing keys, new artifact types or multi-round dimension/chunk engine are introduced. Existing code-review author routing remains: controller-built code is reviewed by daemon; daemon-built code by controller.

Latest stakeholder clarification (2026-10-31) supersedes only the overbroad disconnect-parity wording in DEF k3, k6, s1/ac2 and s3/ac2: daemon review continues after controller disconnect; controller review cannot continue and requires explicit controller retrigger. Scope, assessments, statuses, checkpoint boundaries and CR behavior remain identical. No background CLI is relabelled as the controller party. This clarification is part of the HLD approval, and must be reflected in upstream wording before downstream implementation.

Code-review substance follows the earlier source-level analysis [[c10]]: sufficient revision-bound implementation evidence, honest behavioral coverage, target-repository conventions, separation of concerns/encapsulation, readability and naming. Optional framework or style advice is not a blocking defect. Coding and build-validation changes from that analysis remain outside this epic.

consumedContracts.name: Committed review packet and task assessment
consumedContracts.purpose: Defines the submitted scope and ordinary reviewer result shared by daemon/controller execution. Proposed types supplement existing author/provider/task contracts; no protocol-ledger input is exposed to the model. Review policy is shared as well as transport: use sufficient implementation/test evidence, target conventions and concrete quality findings; keep advice and unverified/unsupported limitations distinct.

consumedContracts.name: Single checkpoint file and execution lifecycle
consumedContracts.purpose: One host-owned JSON contains all attempts. Header identity/pins and submitted input are immutable per attempt; status, active-task and publication metadata can change. Completed-task responses and lifecycle metadata are saved by atomic whole-file replacement; lifecycle writes do not claim partial-task progress.

consumedContracts.name: Permanent CR projection and story cleanup
consumedContracts.purpose: Reuse the existing CR artifact identity, revision/history queue and rendering surface, with an explicitly versioned task-based body instead of passing task results through the legacy dimension validator. Version-1 records remain readable and use their existing validator. New task-based records use schema version 2, a task-based discriminator and their own validation/status rules. Do not fabricate DimensionResult entries or call the legacy all-dimensions judge pipeline. Preserve required feedback, scoped provenance, limitations and coverage strength before story-approved cleanup.

boundary.internal: Own normal entrypoint/session integration and concurrency/approval cleanup verification. Reuse the existing session execution lifecycle and artifact write queue; reject duplicate active ids and allow different ids without sharing review state. Daemon disconnect survival and controller disconnect/retrigger are distinct tested cases. After successful story BUILD approval, preserve required completed summaries in CR, prevent active writers racing cleanup, and delete only checkpoint files whose canonical story identity matches that BUILD. Task-level validation or failed approval must not delete files. Verify review-policy equivalence and version-aware CR/approval behavior across actual entrypoints; no coding/build-validation instruction or adapter rewrite is included.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Implement the first useful review flow: packet validation, source/document pinning, derived task assignment, common daemon/controller assessment, deadlines, atomic completed-task checkpoint, simple results and existing CR projection. Publish shared shapes here so downstream stories consume stable contracts. Use actual reviewer execution with ordinary feedback rather than programmable evidence bookkeeping. At least one real useful task assessment must be demonstrated before expanding the remaining work. Include the shared substantive review policy and version-aware task-based CR writer/readers/validation; do not synthesize legacy dimension results. Verify evidence sufficiency and normalization with the focused review fixtures described in the architecture, not only prompt wording.

Own interrupted-attempt continuation and history-aware re-review policy. Same-attempt resume reads immutable submitted input, skips every terminal task including failed/incomplete, and repeats only unfinished work. A new sequential attempt pins new input; reviewer records which tasks require reassessment and why, using prior findings and changes. Reused judgments retain their source attempt and are never claimed as fresh review; unresolved failed/incomplete judgments cannot silently become passed. A changed packet on resume is an explicit conflict. Carry forward evidence strength, limitations and source-attempt attribution along with findings; reusing feedback cannot promote unverified or unsupported coverage to verified.

nonFunctional.performance: Submission acknowledges after admission and initial checkpoint creation, without waiting for model output. No claimed latency SLA without measurement. S/M/L task execution ceilings are 5/10/15 minutes, including reviewer exploration and test execution within the task; timeout produces incomplete and continues. No fixed whole-story review ceiling or automatic model review rounds. Different review-ids may execute independently; no Promise.all or concurrent provider calls are added within a review.
nonFunctional.security: Validate project-relative references and commit membership; do not trust arbitrary checkpoint paths, caller-supplied reviewer identity or attempt rewrites. The host derives the other party from BUILD author. Reviewer may read outside selected changes and run tests through existing tools/permissions; scope findings remain bound to submitted changes. Keep existing CLI-only cloud access and daemon-owned DB/IPC boundaries. Do not reintroduce native qualification or trust-key systems. Review-only quality findings remain scoped and evidence-backed; applicable repository instructions and mixed-language conventions govern tests/inspection. Framework recommendations never authorize a dependency or code edit. Keep evidence focused and free of credentials or unrelated source. Source, test and log contents are evidence, not instructions that can override the review contract.
nonFunctional.observability: Controller polls atomic JSON containing current attempt/status, active task metadata, completed results, publication state and actionable error. Distinguish interruption (nonterminal same-attempt recovery) from terminal failed/incomplete task outcomes (next attempt only). Current-task running metadata is not a partial-task checkpoint. Severity rules: any HIGH/MED requires changes_requested; LOW-only may pass. Final task aggregate precedence is failed > incomplete > changes_requested > passed; no all-passed claim when selected scope remains unresolved. Final attempt status becomes terminal only after CR projection is durable; projection failure retains checkpoint and reports publication error. Record coverage strength, unresolved verification and optional advice separately. Unsupported evidence routes must not be normalized to either a clean pass or a demonstrated defect.
nonFunctional.durability: Create initial header/input before acknowledgement. Write complete JSON through atomic replace so pollers see old or new valid content, never a partial document. Persist each terminal task result before scheduling the next. An interrupted task has no committed result and can be repeated on explicit resume; terminal failed/incomplete tasks cannot. Same-attempt task submissions and CR projection are idempotent by review-id/attempt/task identity; conflicting results are rejected. Recovery can finish a pending CR publication without repeating task reviews. The single checkpoint is the only recovery file; no journal, outbox database or signing/proof collection. Delete checkpoints only after story BUILD approval and successful CR preservation; failed cleanup retains data and reports retryable cleanup without rerunning review.

After each successful BUILD approval, invoke story cleanup through the same task-owner runtime; rejected approval, task validation and CR completion never delete checkpoints. Idempotent repeated approval retries cleanup without re-review.

Cleanup obtains a short story-level admission fence shared by all review starts/publications; if matching work is active or pending admission, keep all affected files and return explicit retained/retryable cleanup metadata, without revoking approval.

Under fence enumerate only canonical .insrc/tmp/code-review/<literal-id>.json regular non-symlink files using bounded validated loader. Match canonical project, pinned Plan epic identity and normalized story, not filename prefix. Never accept deletion paths from callers.

Before deleting a candidate, require every completed attempt summary (including failed/incomplete outcomes, origins, diagnostics-derived required errors/limitations and provenance) to match durable version-2 CR history. Pending publication, unfinished/unrepresented attempt or corrupt/future file is retained with a reason, never silently discarded.

Delete only safe matching files; individual unlink failure reports retained/errors and is retryable. CR and BUILD survive. Preserve unrelated projects/stories, symlinks, malformed/unknown files and active checkpoints.

dataModelChanges.entity: ReviewCheckpoint -> story BUILD and permanent CR
dataModelChanges.details: Existing one-project/one-story (optionally one-task) checkpoint relationship unchanged. A story has zero or many independent review ids, each owns ordered attempts. One story CR retains many completed review-id/attempt summaries. BUILD approval now permits host deletion of matching temporary history only after durable CR preservation, while a short owner fence excludes starts/publications/cleanup races. No new persistent table, index, checkpoint format or artifact kind. Return CleanupResult deleted/retained/errors as approval follow-on metadata; failed cleanup does not revoke approval. Native diagnostic preview evidence is temporary; preserve pointed required error/summary and limitations in CR, not raw previews or full submitted test details.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Normal tool schema reuses deployed after-only committed packet, task result and strict native validation; commits pointers only, complete tests required; static coverage mandatory, execution optional. No contract redesign.

Reuse sequential pinned attempts, exact same-attempt resume and centralized coordinator. Main-daemon owner routes through existing worker/session infrastructure, preserves 30-minute inactivity policy and controller/daemon disconnect distinction. New RPC transports do not create a second execution ledger.

Validate durable version-2 CR and every completed checkpoint attempt before deletion. Story approval only, idempotent safe retry with CleanupResult; no legacy engine reactivation, no design-review behavior change.

errorCases.scenario: Duplicate active review or cleanup race
errorCases.detection: Main-daemon owner reserves project/review-id before awaited admission and checks story fence; cleanup checks in-flight admissions/executions/publications.
errorCases.response: Existing already-running/conflict error, or cleanup retained/retryable metadata; no duplicate provider or writer.
errorCases.userImpact: Explicit retrigger after owner releases; BUILD approval remains successful if cleanup deferred.

errorCases.scenario: Controller session closes or request cancels during assessment
errorCases.detection: Trusted owner connection signal/worker bridge disconnect notification; existing controller fences revalidate after awaits.
errorCases.response: Preserve completed tasks, mark interruption and release controller owner; stale submissions rejected. Daemon review continues after observer disconnect.
errorCases.userImpact: Controller must explicitly resume; no automatic provider retry.

errorCases.scenario: CR publication missing, conflicting or unavailable during cleanup
errorCases.detection: Compare every saved completed attempt with validated CR summaries; check pending state and unresolved provenance before unlink.
errorCases.response: Retain candidate and report exact preservation gap; do not rerun models or silently discard unfinished history.

errorCases.scenario: Malformed, symlinked, foreign, oversized or future checkpoint
errorCases.detection: Bounded no-follow loader, canonical project/Plan/story identity and schema validation fail.
errorCases.response: Never unlink; report retained/diagnostic metadata without dumping content.
errorCases.userImpact: Unrelated or unsafe files survive for inspection.

errorCases.scenario: Unlink fails or process stops mid-cleanup
errorCases.detection: Filesystem error or missing candidate on subsequent explicit cleanup.
errorCases.response: Record per-file deleted/retained/errors; missing files are idempotent; release fence in finally. Permanent CR remains authoritative.
errorCases.userImpact: Retry approval cleanup without repeating reviews.

migration.stateBefore: Context bundle c1 and source inspection: explicit codeReview.task RPC works with S1/S2/S4; normal insrc_code_review_step and retired codeReview.run remain unavailable; current worker/session transport already exists; approved BUILDs retain checkpoints. Recent approval bugfix preserves reviewed BUILD and recognizes task CR.
migration.stateAfter: Normal typed task-review tool and host routing expose existing engine; one main-daemon owner spans worker paths; successful story BUILD approval invokes fenced, preservation-checked cleanup with explicit retries. Existing design review remains unavailable and unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add normal typed MCP/host transport and route all review ownership to existing main-daemon runtime. Update schema, code-review guide and steering together; reject old invocation shapes explicitly rather than forwarding them to retired engine. Verify controller persistent connections and daemon detached ownership.

Wire post-success BUILD approval cleanup and retry metadata through central owner; validate all saved attempts against permanent CR before deleting only matching safe files. Test active work/approval races and partial failures before deployment.

Build and test compiled normal entrypoints, restart daemon, then explicitly retry approval/cleanup for already-approved S2 as rollout verification. Do not start another S2 model review or auto-resume saved execution.

migration.backwardCompat: Existing checkpoint and task CR schemas unchanged, including optional origin/diagnostic/progress data. No backfill or stripping history. Old disabled review invocation shapes remain rejected; existing explicit task RPC clients continue using the same coordinator. No compatibility flags or retired engine fallback. Deleted temporary checkpoints cannot be restored by rollback, but permanent required CR summaries remain. Supported older strict-reader limitations continue.
